(Charlotte, North Carolina) | college = [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]] (2004–2008) | draft_year = 2008 | career_start = 2008 | career_end = 2017 | career_position = [[Shooting guard]] | career_number = 22, 23, 3, 2, 11 | years1 = {{nbay|2008|start}}–{{nbay|2009|end}} | team1 = [[Golden State Warriors]] | years2 = {{nbay|2010|start}}–{{nbay|2011|end}} | team2 = [[New Jersey Nets]] | years3 = {{nbay|2012|full=y}} | team3 = [[Atlanta Hawks]] | years4 = {{nbay|2012|end}} | team4 = [[Dallas Mavericks]] | years5 = {{nbay|2013|full=y}} | team5 = [[New Orleans Pelicans]] | years6 = {{nbay|2014|start}}–{{nbay|2016|end}} | team6 = [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] | years7 = {{nbay|2016|end}} | team7 = [[Chicago Bulls]] | highlights = * [[North Carolina Mr. Basketball]] (2004) }} {{confused|Anthony Morrow (Royal Navy officer)}} '''Anthony Jarrad Morrow''' (born September 27, 1985) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player and executive who was most recently an executive for the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).{{Cite web|title=Nick Collison To Take On New Role In Thunder Front Office|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-collison-210810|url-status=live|access-date=November 9, 2021|website=Oklahoma City Thunder|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210810163103/https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-collison-210810 |archive-date=August 10, 2021 }} He played [[college basketball]] for [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]]. He went undrafted in the [[2008 NBA draft]] but was later signed by the [[Golden State Warriors]]. He was best known for his three-point shooting.{{Cite news|url=https://www.welcometoloudcity.com/2014/7/12/5893785/anthony-morrow-three-point-shooter-oklahoma-city-thunder-free-agency|title=What the Morrow signing means for the Thunder|work=Welcome to Loud City|access-date=2018-09-15}} ==College career== Morrow played four years of college basketball for [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]], where in 123 games, he made 70 starts and averaged 11.4 points, 3.3 rebounds and 1.0 assists per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/anthony-morrow-1.html|title=Anthony Morrow|work=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=January 1, 2019}} ==Professional career== ===Golden State Warriors (2008–2010)=== [[File:Anthony Morrow contesting Allen Iverson shot.jpg|thumb|upright|Morrow contests an Allen Iverson shot in 2010]] After going undrafted in the [[2008 NBA draft]], Morrow joined the [[Golden State Warriors]] for the 2008 NBA Summer League. On July 24, 2008, he signed with the Warriors.[http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Anthony-Morrow/Summary/864 Anthony Morrow Player Profile – RealGM]{{Cite news|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/117341-anthony-morrow-a-pleasant-surprise-in-an-otherwise-dismal-season-for-warriors|title=Anthony Morrow: A Pleasant Surprise in an Otherwise Dismal Warriors Season|last=Ramirez|first=Jordan|work=Bleacher Report|access-date=2018-09-15}} In his first NBA start, he scored 37 points on 15-for-20 shooting against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]—the most points ever scored in a game by an undrafted player in his rookie season—and grabbed 11 rebounds.[https://web.archive.org/web/20081207000633/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=281115012 Rookie Morrow explodes for 37 points, 11 boards in 1st NBA start] Morrow finished the 2008–09 season as the first rookie and first Warrior ever to lead the league in three-point field goal shooting, going 86-for-184 for a .467 percentage.[http://www.sfgate.com/warriors/article/A-rookie-whose-3-point-stroke-leads-the-league-3245064.php A rookie whose 3-point stroke leads the league] Morrow re-joined the Warriors for the [[NBA Summer League|2009 NBA Summer League]], where he scored 47 points for the Warriors in a game against the [[New Orleans Hornets]] – setting the record for the most points scored by an individual in a game at the NBA Summer League.{{cite news |last1=Brown |first1=Daniel |title=Remembering a Warriors record-setting summer-league debut overshadowing Steph Curry |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7448697/2026/07/16/warriors-anthony-morrow-nba-summer-league-steph-curry/ |access-date=19 July 2026 |work=The New York Times |date=16 July 2026}}{{Cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?page=090716vegassummerleaguegswnorrecap|title=Warriors' Morrow nets Summer-League best 47|date=2009-07-17|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2018-09-15}} In the 13th game of the [[2009–10 NBA season]], Morrow set a new career high with 6 three-pointers in a victory over the Dallas Mavericks.[https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2009112406 Ellis, Morrow lead Warriors past Mavericks 111-103] ===New Jersey Nets (2010–2012)=== On July 13, 2010, Morrow signed a 3-year, $12 million contract with the [[New Jersey Nets]], with Golden State matching the offer, but he was subsequently traded to the Nets for a future second-round draft pick in a [[sign-and-trade]] deal.{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/Nets_Acquire_Guard_Anthony_Morrow.html | title=Nets Acquire Guard Anthony Morrow | work=NBA.com | date=July 13, 2010 | access-date=February 22, 2013}} At the end of the 2010–11 NBA season, Morrow had the second highest 3-point percentage in history (behind [[Steve Kerr]]).{{cite web|last=Stephenson|first=Colin|title=Nets' Anthony Morrow has mastered the art of the 3-point shot after years of practice|url=http://www.nj.com/nets/index.ssf/2011/03/nets_anthony_morrow_has_master.html|work=NJ.com|date=March 29, 2011|access-date=January 15, 2014}} On February 3, 2012, Morrow scored a career-high 42 points in a loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves.[http://www.northjersey.com/sports/Nets_let_Anthony_Morrows_career-high_42-point_effort_go_to_waste.html Nets let Anthony Morrow's career-high 42-point effort go to waste] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120210234817/http://www.northjersey.com/sports/Nets_let_Anthony_Morrows_career-high_42-point_effort_go_to_waste.html |date=2012-02-10 }} ===Atlanta Hawks (2012–2013)=== On July 11, 2012, the Nets traded Morrow, [[Johan Petro]], [[Jordan Farmar]], [[Jordan Williams (basketball, born 1990)|Jordan Williams]], and [[DeShawn Stevenson]] to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] for [[Joe Johnson (basketball)|Joe Johnson]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/two-major-transactions-significantly-reshape-hawks-future | title=Two Major Transactions Significantly Reshape Hawks Future |work=NBA.com|date=July 11, 2012 | access-date=July 11, 2012}} ===Dallas Mavericks (2013)=== On February 21, 2013, the Atlanta Hawks traded Morrow to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for [[Dahntay Jones]].{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/mavericks/post/_/id/4694508/sources-mavs-acquire-hawks-anthony-morrow-for-dahntay-jones | title=NBA trades - Mavs acquire Anthony Morrow at deadline | work=ESPN.com | date=February 21, 2013 | access-date=January 15, 2014}} ===New Orleans Pelicans (2013–2014)=== [[File:20140101 Anthony Morrow background.JPG|thumb|upright|Morrow with the Pelicans in 2014]] On July 18, 2013, Morrow signed a one-year contract with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-anthony-morrow|title=Pelicans Sign Anthony Morrow|access-date=October 27, 2018}} ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2014–2017)=== On July 16, 2014, Morrow signed a three-year, $10 million contract with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].[http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release_morrow_140716 "Thunder Signs Anthony Morrow"]. NBA.com. Retrieved September 20, 2016[http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/234253/Thunder-Agree-To-Sign-Anthony-Morrow-On-Three-Year-$10M-Deal Thunder Agree To Sign Anthony Morrow On Three-Year, $10M Deal] On April 1, 2015, he scored a season-high 32 points on 11-of-16 shooting in a loss to the Dallas Mavericks.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150401/DALOKC/gameinfo.html |title=Mavs beat Thunder 135-131 despite Westbrook triple-double |access-date=2015-04-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202103441/http://www.nba.com/games/20150401/DALOKC/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2017-02-02 |url-status=dead }} On January 4, 2016, Morrow scored a season-high 20 points in a loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160104/SACOKC/gameinfo.html|title=Cousins has 33 points, 19 boards, Kings top Thunder 116-104|work=NBA.com|date=January 4, 2016|access-date=January 4, 2016}} ===Chicago Bulls (2017)=== On February 23, 2017, Morrow was traded, along with [[Joffrey Lauvergne]] and [[Cameron Payne]], to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in exchange for [[Taj Gibson]], [[Doug McDermott]] and a [[Mitchell Robinson|2018 second-round draft pick]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-acquire-payne-morrow-and-lauvergne-thunder|title=Bulls acquire Payne, Morrow, and Lauvergne from Thunder|work=NBA.com|date=February 23, 2017|access-date=February 23, 2017}} On September 18, 2017, Morrow signed with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-anthony-morrow|title=Trail Blazers Sign Anthony Morrow|work=NBA.com|date=September 18, 2017|access-date=September 18, 2017}} He was waived on October 13 after appearing in five preseason games.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-waive-briscoe-goodwin-and-morrow|title=Trail Blazers Waive Briscoe, Goodwin and
